title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — U.S. Government Defense Environment Overview (DoD and NASA appropriations, funded programs)
key_points: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 provided FY2023 appropriations including $817 billion for the U.S. DoD and $25.4 billion for NASA.
FY23 appropriations included funding for Boeing's major programs: F/A-18 Super Hornet, F-15EX, CH-47 Chinook, AH-64 Apache, V-22 Osprey, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25, and the Space Launch System.
FY23 appropriations support F/A-18 production further into calendar year 2025 and did not include funding for additional P-8 aircraft.
There is ongoing uncertainty regarding program-level appropriations for the U.S. DoD, NASA and other government agencies for fiscal year 2024 and beyond.
raw_excerpt: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, enacted in December 2022, provided fiscal year 2023 (FY23) appropriations for government departments and agencies, including $817 billion for the U.S. DoD and $25.4 billion for NASA. The enacted FY23 appropriations included funding for Boeing's major programs, including the F/A-18 Super Hornet, F-15EX, CH-47 Chinook, AH-64 Apache, V-22 Osprey, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25, and the Space Launch System.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Note: KC-46A Tanker and T-7A Red Hawk contracts with the U.S. Air Force
key_points: In 2011 Boeing was awarded a contract from the USAF to design, develop, manufacture and deliver four next-generation aerial refueling tankers, plus priced options for 13 annual production lots totaling 179 aircraft.

Since 2016 the USAF has authorized eight low rate initial production (LRIP) lots for a total of 109 aircraft; the EMD contract and authorized LRIP lots total approximately $21 billion as of December 31, 2022.
Boeing increased the reach-forward loss on the KC-46A Tanker program by $1,374M during 2022, reflecting higher production and supply chain costs.

In 2018 Boeing was awarded the T-7A Red Hawk program; the EMD portion is an $860M fixed-price contract covering five aircraft and seven simulators, with 11 production lots for 346 aircraft in the production portion.
Boeing recorded 2022 earnings charges of $203M on T-7A EMD and $552M on T-7A production options.
raw_excerpt: In 2011, we were awarded a contract from the USAF to design, develop, manufacture, and deliver four next generation aerial refueling tankers as well as priced options for 13 annual production lots totaling 179 aircraft. … Since 2016, the USAF has authorized eight low rate initial production (LRIP) lots for a total of 109 aircraft. The EMD contract and authorized LRIP lots total approximately $21 billion as of December 31, 2022.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Note: Commercial Crew (CST-100 Starliner) contract with NASA
key_points: NASA contracted Boeing to design and build the CST-100 Starliner spacecraft to transport crews to the International Space Station.
Boeing completed the uncrewed Orbital Flight Test in the second quarter of 2022; a crewed flight test was expected in 2023.

Boeing increased the Commercial Crew reach-forward loss by $288M during 2022, reflecting higher estimated costs to complete crewed flight tests and revised schedules for the crewed flight test and three post-certification missions.
raw_excerpt: NASA has contracted us to design and build the CST-100 Starliner spacecraft to transport crews to the International Space Station. During the second quarter of 2022 we successfully completed the uncrewed Orbital Flight Test. A crewed flight test is now expected to be completed in 2023. During the year ended December 31, 2022, we increased the reach-forward loss by $288 primarily reflecting increases to estimated costs related to completing the crewed flight tests and revised schedules for both the crewed flight test and three post certification missions.

title: Boeing FY2022 Form 10-K — 737 Program: China delivery status and China-designated inventory
key_points: Over 190 countries have approved resumption of 737 MAX operations; the first 737 MAX passenger flight in China since 2019 occurred on January 13, 2023 (after the FY2022 reporting period).
There is uncertainty regarding timing of resumption of deliveries in China, which remain subject to final regulatory approvals.
Boeing had approximately 250 aircraft in inventory as of December 31, 2022, including approximately 140 aircraft designated for customers in China.
Boeing is remarketing some of the China-designated aircraft to other customers and anticipates delivering most inventory aircraft by the end of 2024.
Boeing continues to work with a small number of customers who have requested to defer deliveries or cancel 737 MAX orders.
